claims.text: Adding a small amount of a liquid-phase-forming sintering aid to ceramic powder reduces the sintering temperature.
A sintering aid promotes enhanced grain-boundary diffusion and mass transport during densification.
A small percentage of a transition-metal oxide or low-melting-point additive can serve as the sintering aid.
The sintering aid forms a transient liquid phase localized at grain boundaries during heat treatment.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport and diffusion at grain boundaries.
The sintering aid lowers the activation energy required for densification.
Enhanced grain-boundary transport permits effective ceramic sintering at a reduced temperature.
Aid-containing samples will achieve densification comparable to undoped samples at a lower sintering temperature.
Aid-containing samples will achieve microstructural uniformity comparable to undoped samples at a lower sintering temperature.
The beneficial effect is limited to a certain range of sintering-aid concentrations.
Excessive sintering-aid concentrations may produce unwanted secondary phases.
Excessive sintering-aid concentrations may degrade material properties.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction and the optimum dopant concentration depend on the ceramic system and sintering conditions.
